label: copy-phase input n echoed early (1st-2nd output fed back) in longer sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is n, and only early in the copy (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. the input is original token 0 or 1 being echoed back). It never fires on n during the original phase or at the delimiter, and never on any other input token. The largest activations come when n is the first original token and is fed back at the first copy step (recall_idx 1) in long sequences (L = 8-9). Activations are roughly half as large when n is original token 1 (recall_idx 2), weak and sparse at recall_idx 3 (about 1.6% of mass), and absent later. Short sequences (L <= 4) mostly do not activate, and activation grows with L / outputs remaining.

issues: The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says activations at recall_idx 2 are 'roughly half as large' as at recall_idx 1. Dev profile: recall_idx 1 has 13,921 active steps holding 0.488 of activation mass, and recall_idx 2 has 13,235 active steps holding 0.496, so the mean per active step is the same or slightly higher at recall_idx 2. Test split: recall_idx==1 gives recall 0.485 / mass 0.493, and recall_idx==2 gives recall 0.452 / mass 0.492. For L>=8 alone: recall_idx 1 gives recall 0.189 / mass 0.300, and recall_idx 2 gives recall 0.191 / mass 0.283. The top-12 examples are all recall_idx 1 at about 0.9 of max, so recall_idx 1 owns the extreme tail. The visible halving (0.91 then 0.44) appears only in 'n n ...' sequences, where n is both token 0 and token 1. On average the two positions are about equal.

The core claims check out. All activation mass is in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases are 0). in_tok is n for 100% of activations. Mass by recall_idx is 0.488 / 0.496 / 0.016 for 1 / 2 / 3 and 0 from 4 on. Mass rises with L and with to_go. Reported test scores reproduce: P 0.947, R 0.892, F1 0.918, mass recall 0.971.

The remaining misses and false positives are a graded boundary, not a separate class. Misses are weak firings on n at recall_idx 3 in L=7-8 sequences and at recall_idx 1 in L=4 sequences, together 2.9% of mass. False positives are mostly n at recall_idx 2 in L=5 sequences (to_go=2). Changing the boundary did not help on test: L>=6 F1 0.854, to_go>=3 F1 0.885, an L-dependent split F1 0.890, adding recall_idx 3 at L>=8 F1 0.881. All are below the original 0.918, so the original predicate is about as good as this variable set allows.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input n when it echoes original token 0 or 1 (recall_idx 1-2) in sequences of length 5 or more; both positions have similar magnitude, and activation grows with outputs remaining
